titulo: Baseline: why almost every click is branded
lead: The total clicks in Search Console are misleading. At the start, almost every click comes from people who already typed your name. That click is good, but it doesn't show whether your SEO works. In this lesson you pull a 28-day baseline and separate the brand from the rest, as INEMA did in September 2026.
objetivo: pull the 28-day baseline and separate how many clicks come from people who already search for your name.

aprende.t: Why the total clicks are misleading
The three buckets: branded, non-branded, and anonymized
Write your brand regex in the dashboard filter
Record the baseline to compare a month from now

hero_alt: A woman draws a horizontal line in pencil on graph paper, next to a laptop showing a bar chart.

nos.detalhe: Clicks and impressions from the Performance report, Web tab. It's the sum of everything: people who searched for your name, people who searched for a topic, and the queries Google hides.
Queries with your name, your site's name, or typos of it. These visitors were already looking for you: the click would come with or without SEO.
Topic queries ("free ai course", "how to learn ai"). This is where people who didn't know you found you. It's the number that shows whether SEO is working.
Rare queries don't appear in the table, for privacy, but they count toward the total. That's why the total isn't equal to branded plus non-branded: the difference is the anonymized queries.

secoes.legenda: Total minus branded minus non-branded gives you the anonymized queries. Write down all three numbers, not just the total.

secoes.sub: All in the dashboard, no script. Click each step.

texto: In Search Console, open Performance, Search results. Choose the last 28 days and check clicks, impressions, CTR, and position.
Write down the total. It's the starting point, not the result.
Write your brand regex: the name, the domain, variations, and typos, separated by a vertical bar.
In the Query filter, choose the custom (regex) option and "matches". Write down clicks and impressions.
Switch the filter to "doesn't match" the same regex. Write it down again.
Add branded and non-branded and subtract from the total: what's left is the anonymized queries.
Save the numbers in a spreadsheet with the date of the window. Four weeks from now, you compare the same 28-day window.
Without the record, improvement becomes a personal impression.

exemplo.texto: inema.club had 787 clicks and a 34% CTR. It looked great. But 639 of the 647 clicks from the top searches were branded; non-branded searches added up to just 8 clicks and 72 impressions.

28-day window, 08/25 to 09/21/2026. In the top searches, 639 of 647 clicks were branded. Non-branded searches: 8 clicks and 72 impressions.

• A 34% CTR is high because people who search for your name click on your own site.
  • 8 non-branded clicks in 28 days: that is your real starting point.
  • Goal of the baseline: measure only the non-branded part, because the brand dominates the total and hides the effect of new pages.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Your site has a 34% CTR and an average position of 5.2. Is the SEO working?
opcoes: Yes, a high CTR proves it works.
You can't tell without separating the brand: people who search for your name click on your site.
No, a CTR above 30% is an error.
perguntas.explica: At INEMA, a 34% CTR coexisted with 8 non-branded clicks in 28 days. The total mixes in people who already knew you.

perguntas.p: Why don't branded + non-branded add up to the total?
opcoes: Rare queries are hidden from the table but count in the total: those are the anonymized ones.
perguntas.explica: Google anonymizes rare queries. They count in the total and disappear from the query filter.

perguntas.p: What goes in the brand regex?
opcoes: Name, domain, variations and common typos.
perguntas.explica: Someone who types "inema clube" is looking for the brand. If the variation is left out, the brand leaks into the non-branded bucket and inflates the number.

perguntas.p: To compare a month from now, what do you need to keep?
opcoes: The window dates and the numbers for the three buckets, from the same 28-day window.
Nothing: the dashboard keeps it forever.
perguntas.explica: Same window, same buckets. And the dashboard doesn't keep it forever: the history disappears after about 16 months (lesson 8).

itens.texto: At the start, almost every click comes from people already searching for your name.
Branded, non-branded, and anonymized. What matters is non-branded.
The generative AI report in Search Console shows impressions only. The click baseline is still the Performance report.
